records.name: Trinity Kristen School of the Arts
records.summary: A dance school for kids, teens and adults, with classes in ballet, hip-hop, tap, jazz and modern. The school says no experience is needed to start.
records.what_you_do: Take a dance class. Kids and teens can try ballet, hip-hop, tap, jazz or modern. Adults can join hip-hop, Zumba, heels, pole, ballet or jazz classes.

schedule.text: Studio open weekly: Monday to Wednesday 3 to 8 pm, Friday 6 to 8 pm for adults, and Saturday 11 am to 5 pm.

cost.text: Registration is $30 online, or $20 if you register early, by September 1, for the 2026 to 2027 season. A $20 sibling discount is available by contacting the school. Paying for the year up front takes $40 off each child. Monthly tuition is not listed on the site.

access.notes: The studio is on the second floor of the building.

first_step.how: Register through the Sign Up Now button on the price list page, or call 267-736-1738 with questions before you pay.
first_step.basis: The school says no experience is needed, offers a sign up button, and lists a phone line. The site does not describe a trial class.
first_step.what_to_expect: The school describes its classes as nurturing and not competitive. Kids and teens choose from ballet, hip-hop, tap, jazz or modern, and adults can pick from several styles. The site does not say how long a class runs or what a first class looks like, so call before you sign up.
first_visit_tips: The studio is on the second floor of 6508 Woodland Ave.
Friday evening hours are for adults only, so check which class fits before you come.
The site does not list a dress code or shoes, so ask what to wear before the first class.

records.notes: Hours and prices come from the school's own pages, checked 2026-10-08. The price list names the 2026 to 2027 season but gives no month, so last_sign_of_life is left out and status stays probably_active. The contact page email uses a different domain (trinitykschoolotheart.org) from the website, so it is not recorded. The summer camp page shows no dates (only a 2024 copyright footer) and was not used. The about page has no dated news.

records.name: Women of Many Hats
records.summary: A Christian-based group that supports sheltered services helping families move toward stability, with a focus on women who have survived domestic violence. It also holds an event called the Show Me Love Luncheon.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer, give a monthly gift through the Partner Circle, or donate. The Aid Distribution Program gives out food, diapers, formula and clothing, but the site does not say how to ask for it.

cost.text: Volunteering and the newsletter cost nothing. The Partner Circle sign up form asks whether you would give $10 a month, and you can answer no.

first_step.how: Call 215-240-1361 to say you want to volunteer, and ask how the Aid Distribution Program takes requests.
first_step.basis: The site has a Get Involved page, a public phone line and an email address, so the way in is clear. It does not explain how a volunteer shift works or how aid requests are taken.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a typical volunteer shift. Some volunteer jobs need a background check and child clearance, though the site does not say which jobs. Ask on the phone which roles are open and what a first day involves.
first_visit_tips: Ask which volunteer jobs need a background check and child clearance before you sign up.
Call before you come, since the site does not list volunteer hours or a shift schedule.

records.notes: Partner Circle, Aid Distribution Program and phone line come from the group's own pages. The news page lists items by month and day only (July, August, September), with no year, so none counts as dated evidence and last_sign_of_life is left out. The contact page gives a Chestnut Street office with a suite number that looks like a mailbox, so it is not added as a place to visit. The mailto link on the contact page points to a placeholder address, so the visible info address was used. Shelter services appear only in the founder's bio; there is no shelter page. The aid page gives no eligibility rules, no request steps and no hours. The site does not describe a volunteer shift.

records.name: YOURpath for Adult Learners
records.summary: A nonprofit offering online study help for the GED, HiSET, and TABE tests, plus literacy, math, digital skills, and job readiness courses. The classes are open to adults across the country who did not finish high school or have low reading skills, and they run online at any hour.
records.what_you_do: Start with a free practice test or enroll in an online course from the Enroll Here page, then study on your own schedule. The Next Step program can help with college applications, financial aid and job skills.

schedule.text: Online courses are open around the clock, so you study when it suits you.

cost.text: Free practice tests are offered, and the site says testing fees can be reimbursed up to 100 percent. Course fees are not listed on the site.

first_step.how: Take one of the free practice tests the site offers, then open the Enroll Here page and fill out the enrollment form linked there.
first_step.basis: Adults can start through a public enroll page and free practice tests, with no in person step listed. The site gives no prices, course length or start dates.
first_step.what_to_expect: Courses are self-paced and run online on a computer, tablet or phone at any hour. The site describes tutoring, progress checks and one on one guidance. It does not say how long a course takes or what it costs, so check before you enroll.
first_visit_tips: Have a computer, tablet or phone with internet access ready before you start.
Take a free practice test first to see where you stand.
Ask about course length and fees before you enroll, since the site does not list them.

records.notes: This is an online program for adults anywhere, run from a Philadelphia address (8122 Buist Ave). A reviewer may decide it is out of area rather than a Philadelphia group. It stays publish because the organization is based in Philadelphia and Philadelphia adults can enroll. The licensing page lists yearly organization licenses from $1,200 to $18,000; those are for programs, not learners, so they are not in cost. The contact page has a form only, with no published phone or email. It lists office hours of 9 am to 5 pm without days. Two earlier duplicate address entries were merged into one.

records.name: Ardella's House
records.summary: A nonprofit that helps women and girls with criminal justice histories find work, housing, and health care, and rebuild family life. It runs housing for women coming home from incarceration, job training, mentoring, and reentry classes.
records.what_you_do: Fill out the Volunteer Interest Survey to offer time, or ask for a guest speaker for your group. Women who want housing ask for the application packet by phone or email, then send a questionnaire and a short letter and complete a virtual interview.

cost.text: The site does not list any fees for volunteering, guest speakers or housing.

first_step.how: Fill out the Volunteer Interest Survey linked on the site, or call 267-249-3642 to ask how you can help.
first_step.basis: The volunteer survey is public and easy to find, but the site does not say what happens after you send it. The housing route is longer: a questionnaire, a letter and a required virtual interview.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a volunteer shift or how long a visit takes. Housing works as an application, not a walk in: you request the packet, send it back, and complete a virtual interview before any acceptance. Staff review each application for fit, and accepted women may get help planning their release if they need it.
first_visit_tips: For housing, have your questionnaire and a short letter about your goals ready before you contact staff.
The site lists two phone numbers, 267-249-3642 on the contact page and 267-228-4169 for requesting housing materials. Ask which one fits your question.

records.notes: Housing eligibility from the housing page: women returning from incarceration in the Philadelphia area. No age limit, sobriety rule or required referral source is stated on that page. Two phone numbers are published: 267-249-3642 on the contact page (recorded as phone) and 267-228-4169 under Request Materials on the housing page. A reviewer should confirm which is current. The contact page email is hidden behind protected text, so no email is recorded. The Sisters Empowerment Circle is a monthly donor group, not a program for women served, so it is left out of what_you_do. The annual report link was not opened. The newcomer rating of 3 applies to volunteering; the housing route would rate lower.

records.name: Christian Legal Clinics of Philadelphia
records.summary: Volunteer lawyers give free first consultations and legal help on housing, child custody, domestic abuse, wills, estates, and clearing criminal records, at clinics across the region. The group is a Christian legal ministry, and its clinics also have volunteers who offer prayer and chaplain support.
records.what_you_do: Get legal help by calling 215-399-0064 or filling out the consultation form, and the clinic calls you back. Lawyers can volunteer at a clinic once a month for three to four hours, and non-lawyers can help with prayer, hospitality or chaplain work.

locations.label: Hunting Park clinic (Joy in the City)
South Philadelphia West clinic (Salvation Army Central Corps)
South Philadelphia East clinic (Philadelphia Access Center)

cost.text: The first consultation is free. If a volunteer lawyer cannot take your case, the clinic can sometimes arrange a low cost referral.

first_step.how: Call 215-399-0064 and choose the clinic nearest you, or fill out the Schedule a Consultation form on the site and describe your legal problem.
first_step.basis: Anyone can ask for a consultation by phone or online, and the first one is free. The page does not say who qualifies, and it reports a wait of one to three months.
first_step.what_to_expect: After you send the form, the clinic says it will call you. The site does not say how long that call takes or whether the first meeting is in person. The group describes itself as Christian, and clinic volunteers include chaplains and people who pray. The clinic reports waits of one to three months, and for urgent problems the site suggests other legal aid groups.
first_visit_tips: If you have a pending case, have your household size, income, and the other side's name and contact information ready for the call.
Pick the clinic closest to you when you call, since each clinic has its own phone extension.
If your problem is urgent, ask about other legal aid groups while you wait; the site suggests this itself.

records.notes: Legal topics, the free first consultation and the clinic list come from the group's own pages. The clinic list gave seven sites; the six in Philadelphia and the Chester site were read once from the legal clinics page, so spot check the addresses before posting. Clinic days and hours are not on the site, and eligibility is not stated. The trainings page gives 2023 in the body and 2024 in the event titles, so it was not used as dated evidence. Status and last_sign_of_life are carried from tier 1 (news page, 2026-06) and were not re-checked. The group calls itself a Christian ministry; the site does not say whether clients are asked about religion or whether volunteers must share a faith, so audience.faith is left blank. The mailing P.O. Box is not recorded as a place to visit.

records.name: Ian-Yae's in Touch
records.summary: A nonprofit that helps people experiencing homelessness and families in underserved neighborhoods. Its Community H.U.B. offers meals, a clothing closet, a food pantry, haircuts, and computer use, and volunteers help with year-round street outreach.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer with the street outreach team, which works in all four seasons, or ask about helping at the Community H.U.B. The group also runs a weekly meal on Tuesday evenings.

schedule.text: Community meals every Tuesday at 6:30 pm, and free haircuts every Sunday from 11 am to 2 pm.

cost.text: The site lists free haircuts. It does not show a price for the meals, pantry or clothing closet.

first_step.how: Call 267-254-9531 or use the contact form on the site to ask how to volunteer with street outreach or at the Community H.U.B.
first_step.basis: Meal and haircut times are listed, but the site does not say whether you sign up or walk in. Volunteering goes through a contact form or a phone call.
first_step.what_to_expect: The Tuesday community meal is served outdoors at 20th and Race Streets, and a 2023 news item says it has run for more than ten years and draws about 75 people. With the meal, people can get clothing, personal care items, and referrals to housing, other meal sites and job information. The site does not say how long a meal lasts or whether you can just come.
first_visit_tips: Plan to be at 20th and Race Streets by 6:30 pm on a Tuesday, the listed start time.
Dress for the weather, since the meal is outdoors and goes ahead in any weather.
Call before you come if you want to volunteer, since the site does not say what volunteers do at meals.

records.notes: STATUS FLAG FOR REVIEW: the only dated item found is a 2023 Indego news item, which by the status rule would make this group dormant. The group's own site is undated (its footer reads 2013, which is not evidence). I left tier 1's probably_active unchanged so the owner or a reviewer can decide. The Community H.U.B. street address was not found on the site or in search, so the only street address recorded is the mailing address. The about page lists a food pantry on the 4th Tuesday at 6:30 pm, computer use on Sundays 1 to 5 pm, and a youth movie night on the 4th Friday 6 to 8 pm. That page's layout is garbled, so those times are left out of schedule until confirmed; the meal and haircut times are confirmed on two pages. The site gives no volunteer tasks, office hours or accessibility details. The phone number is from the contact page; the contact page's email address was not recorded.

records.name: Mission of Hope and Redemption
records.summary: A volunteer-run food pantry in Philadelphia where families choose their own groceries. It serves about 200 families a week and also runs outreach with essential supplies and school support.
records.what_you_do: Register in person at the Thursday pantry, then shop for your own food. Volunteers help run the pantry, and the group asks people to reach out through its contact page to join.

schedule.text: Food pantry every Thursday from 11 am to 1:30 pm.

cost.text: The site lists no fee for the pantry.

first_step.how: Go to the pantry on a Thursday between 11 am and 1:30 pm and register in person with your name, address and phone number.
first_step.basis: The pantry has a set day, hours and address, and registration happens when you arrive. The site does not list eligibility rules or a phone line.
first_step.what_to_expect: You register when you arrive, giving your name, address and phone number. Then you pick the foods that fit your household's needs, a shopping style the group calls client choice. The site does not say how long a visit takes, whether bags are given, or what else happens there.
first_visit_tips: Have your name, address and phone number ready for registration.
Bring your own bags, since the site does not say whether bags are provided.
The site does not list eligibility, so ask at the door if you are not sure you qualify.

records.notes: Pantry day, hours and church address come from the Get Help page. The 200 families a week and 15 volunteers come from the About page, which dates neither figure. The About page gives December 2023 as the founding date; that is an origin date, not dated activity, so it did not change status. The contact page has only a Google form, so no phone or email is recorded. The events page lists three event names (a painting event and a back to school giveaway) with no dates, so none was used. The pantry is hosted in a church, and the site does not say whether that matters for who attends. Eligibility is not stated.

notes: Budget: 1 of 1 WebSearch used; 40 WebFetch used (cap 60, max 6 per group, every group within its cap). No page was blocked and no rate limiting was seen. Verdicts: 7 publish, 0 hide. Two items need a reviewer's call: (1) Ian-Yae's in Touch keeps tier 1's probably_active, but its only dated item is a 2023 news item, which by the status rule would be dormant (see that record's notes); (2) Ardella's House lists two different phone numbers on two pages; I recorded the contact page number. Christian Legal Clinics' status is carried from tier 1 and was not re-checked.
